subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can move to the next step (detailed forecast + sample-run):

Pain points you called out:
- Token-driven spend is higher than expected: ~1M calls / month with an average of ~850 tokens per call (prompt + response), driving large monthly inference bills.
- Occasional latency spikes (p90 ~200ms) affecting real-time features.
- Need to keep total inference spend under ~$10k/mo for the pilot.

Goals you mentioned:
- Proof-of-concept to replace current retrieval-based summarization pipeline and hit sub-150ms p95 latency for user-facing flows.
- Demonstrate predictable monthly costs with a path to scale.
- Keep customer data in the US region and meet basic vendor assurance items (we can follow up with security docs).

High-level TCO levers we discussed (attached: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx):
1) Batching/throughput optimization
   - For non-interactive batch workloads, batching can increase GPU utilization and reduce per-token cost by ~20–40% depending on payload distribution.
   - For interactive flows we recommend adaptive batching with a 40–60ms micro-batching window to balance latency and throughput.
2) Prefix/KV caching
   - Many of your calls have repeated system/prompt prefixes. Prefix caching can avoid re-sending/re-computing those tokens (estimated 10–30% token savings on aggregate).
3) Model variant & quantization
   - Running a quantized variant (4-bit) for lower-cost endpoints can reduce model execution cost by ~55–70% with ~small quality delta on many tasks.
4) Autoscaling + reserved capacity tradeoff
   - If you commit to Dedicated reserved capacity, unit $/token falls and latency is more predictable; hosted mode with smart fallbacks keeps ops overhead low.

Rough back-of-envelope numbers (please treat as preliminary):
- Current baseline (your reported): 1,000,000 calls/mo * 850 tokens/call = 850M tokens/mo.
- If run on Redwood hosted default model at ~$0.00002/token -> ~$17,000/mo.
- With a combination of caching (20%), batching/throughput improvements (25% effective), and a quantized variant option for lower-latency paths, we estimate a conservative 60% reduction -> ~$6,800/mo.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- We’ll run a quick sample analysis on a representative set of logs/prompts (please share ~500 representative requests) to produce a 3-tier forecast (pilot / steady / scale).
- Marissa (cc’d) will produce the detailed 3-tier forecast and a configuration comparison (hosted vs dedicated + quantized variants).
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up the week of Nov 16 to review the forecast and procurement questions.

Attachments: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx (summary), we’ll follow with acme-tco-3-tier-forecast.csv once we analyze sample prompts.

If this matches your notes, I’ll have Marissa prepare the forecast and Rafael can do a quick technical runbook for latency tradeoffs.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks Ben — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from my side: 

- Budget constraint: our pilot budget is hard-capped at $10k/month. We can stretch for clear ROI if the forecast is compelling, but baseline needs to be under $10k for procurement to greenlight.
- Request for tiers: please include 3 traffic tiers (50k / 500k / 2M calls per month) with per-month cost, expected p95 latency, and recommended config (hosted vs dedicated).
- Data/assurance: we’ll need SOC2 and data residency confirmation as part of procurement packet — happy to review the template you send.

I’ll put together 500 representative requests and share via S3 link later today. Can you also include an upfront delta between the highest-fidelity model and the 4-bit quantized variant so we can discuss quality tradeoffs with our ML team?

Best,
Sarah
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
sarah.green@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the sample set. I pulled together a short three-tier forecast (attached: acme-tco-3-tier-forecast.csv) and a few clarifying notes on the quality vs cost tradeoffs you asked about. Summary below: 

Three-tier headline (modeling assumptions in attached CSV):
- Low (50k calls/mo): assume interactive profile, low batching, expected tokens/call = 900 -> baseline hosted cost ~$900/mo; optimized hosted with caching + quantized fallback ~$380/mo.
- Mid (500k calls/mo): mix interactive + batch, tokens/call = 850 -> baseline hosted cost ~$9,000/mo; optimized (20% caching + 25% batching + quantized on non-critical paths) ~$3,600/mo.
- High (2M calls/mo): heavy batchable traffic, tokens/call = 800 -> baseline hosted ~$36,000/mo; optimized w/ dedicated reserved capacity + caching ~$12,500/mo.

Quality delta (high-level):
- Full-precision 16-bit model: best quality, higher cost.
- 4-bit quantized variant: estimated ~5–8% degradation on abstractive summarization metrics in internal evals; many customers find this acceptable for lower-sensitivity paths (e.g., system-generated summaries, low-risk assistants).

Latency notes:
- Adaptive micro-batching (40–60ms window) keeps p95 for interactive flows near your 150ms target while enabling batching benefits.
- Dedicated GPU pools reduce tail latency variance — recommended if you need strict SLOs at scale.

Proposed next items (can each be a 30–45m session):
1) We analyze your 500-sample set and run a per-token profile (to be delivered as an annotated CSV).
2) Rafael will run a short latency/throughput test on a representative pipeline (can demo with a small reserved capacity).
3) I’ll share a short A/B eval plan to measure human-perceived quality between full-precision and quantized variants.

If this looks good I’ll:
- Upload the annotated forecast and model-delta report to the shared TCO page (https://redwood.ai/tco/acme-2315).
- Book a follow-up for Nov 17 — here’s my calendar link: https://calendly.com/marissa/redwood-tco-demo

Attachments: acme-tco-3-tier-forecast.csv

Regards,
Marissa Cole
